title: Testing Planck-scale physics: Lorentz invariance violation searches
bottleneck: Quantum gravity is expected to modify physics at the Planck length of 10^-35 meters, some sixteen orders of magnitude below what colliders probe, and no agreed signature survives across candidate theories. Searches for energy-dependent light speed in gamma-ray bursts and modified dispersion relations have found nothing, but the null results only constrain specific models.
why_it_blocks: A scientific theory of quantum gravity must be falsifiable; without any accessible experimental handle, quantum gravity risks remaining metaphysics regardless of its mathematical beauty.
current_state: Astrophysical observations of gamma-ray bursts and cosmic rays place extremely tight bounds on Lorentz violation, while tabletop optomechanical and interferometric experiments probe for Planck-scale spacetime noise with growing sensitivity. Tabletop interferometers and optomechanical resonators now probe for Planck-scale spacetime foam, though no anomaly has survived scrutiny so far.
